observation_summary: The Fraction class fails to correctly reduce fractions when the numerator is Integer.MIN_VALUE, resulting in incorrect values due to overflow or improper GCD calculation.
hypothesis: The greatestCommonDivisor method fails to handle Integer.MIN_VALUE correctly because Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE (due to overflow), causing the existing logic to miscalculate the GCD.
prediction: The code will require a more robust GCD implementation that handles the edge case of Integer.MIN_VALUE explicitly, likely by checking for zero and handling the overflow case before applying standard GCD logic.
experiment_rationale: The fix adds explicit checks for zero and Integer.MIN_VALUE in the greatestCommonDivisor method, ensuring that the GCD calculation does not rely on Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) which is mathematically incorrect for 32-bit signed integers.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the computational logic of the greatestCommonDivisor method. It is not a simple missing guard (Checking) because the logic itself is fundamentally flawed for the specific input range of Integer.MIN_VALUE. It is not an Assignment/Initialization issue because the error is in the procedural calculation of the GCD. Therefore, it is an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The bug report states that greatestCommonDivisor does not find the gcd of Integer.MIN_VALUE and 2^k.
The fix diff adds explicit handling for Integer.MIN_VALUE and zero in the greatestCommonDivisor method.
The failing tests show incorrect results for fractions involving Integer.MIN_VALUE.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks, these are not just guards for null or bounds; they are necessary procedural steps to correctly compute the GCD for edge cases that the original algorithm failed to handle.
